questions.answer: Lead = exactly D cycles (one half period) from o_cs_n fall to SCLK edge 1. Trail = exactly D cycles from SCLK edge 16 to o_cs_n rise. Minimum o_cs_n high time between bursts = at least D cycles (exactly D when the next command is waiting).

Yes. CPOL_b/CPHA_b are captured at the acceptance edge of the first command of a burst, which is the same edge A at which o_cs_n falls. Later changes of i_cpol/i_cpha while o_cs_n = 0 have no effect until o_cs_n rises.

Gapless means a command handshake occurs at edge A+16·D: i_cmd_valid = 1 and o_cmd_ready = 1 in the last cycle of the current transfer. That needs o_rsp_valid = 0 in that cycle and the current transfer's i_cmd_last = 0. Otherwise the burst enters Pause with SCLK idle and o_cs_n low.

Yes. The transfer covers cycles A to A+16·D−1. The last cycle starts at A+16·D−1 and ends at SCLK edge 16, which is edge A+16·D. Trail then lasts D cycles until o_cs_n rises at A+17·D. These are consistent.

D = 1 is legal, giving SCLK = f(i_clk)/2, with lead, trail and gap of 1 cycle. A shift edge and the next sampling edge are 1 cycle apart. No minimum D above 1 is imposed. Silicon timing of i_miso at D = 1 is an integrator duty (ENV-006), and D = 1 stays legal and is verified in simulation.

The input reset value 0 of i_cmd_valid is an environment obligation (ENV-002), not a DUT property. The restriction that i_cpol/i_cpha change only while o_cs_n = 1 is an environment constraint (ENV-003). If it is violated, the master neither detects nor reports it and keeps using CPOL_b/CPHA_b until the end of the burst.
Yes. During reset o_cs_n = 1, so the 'only while o_cs_n = 1' rule allows i_cpol to change. o_sclk must follow it combinationally, and VER-008 toggles i_cpol during reset.

o_cmd_ready = 1 during reset is a reset value only. A command handshake requires i_rst_n = 1, so i_cmd_valid && o_cmd_ready while i_rst_n = 0 is not a handshake and must not be accepted. The checker should treat it as a non-transfer.

After reset release the master is in Idle and can accept a command at the first edge with i_rst_n = 1. This is visible as o_cmd_ready = 1, because o_rsp_valid is 0 after reset. The minimum high time is not enforced across reset.

D is PARA_SPI_CLK_DIV, the number of i_clk cycles in one SCLK half period. It is a fixed elaboration-time parameter in the range 1 to 255, not an input pin, and cannot change at run time. D = 1 is legal and is handled by the same rules.

On i_rst_n assertion, o_cs_n = 1, o_sclk = current i_cpol (combinational), o_cmd_ready = 1, o_mosi = 0, o_rsp_valid = 0 and o_rsp_data = 8'h00. Reset assertion is asynchronous and release is synchronous. Outputs take reset values at once.

No second command can be accepted before o_cs_n rises. In the last cycle of a transfer with captured i_cmd_last = 1, o_cmd_ready = 0. Trail has o_cmd_ready = 0. After o_cs_n rises at R, o_cmd_ready is 0 for cycles R to R+D−2, so the earliest acceptance is R+D.

o_rsp_valid = 1 is first visible in the cycle starting at edge A+16·D, where the byte is loaded (Example 1 shows it in cycle 16). The next transfer, accepted at A+16·D, has its last cycle starting at A+32·D−1. o_rsp_valid must be 0 in that cycle, so the handshake must occur at an edge no later than A+32·D−1. That is 16·D−1 edges after the valid cycle begins.

Yes, the low time includes the lead. o_cs_n falls at the acceptance edge A (0 latency) and rises at A_last+17·D. For n continuous bytes that is 16·n·D + D after A. Of this, the lead D is part of the first 16·D span and the trail D is the extra D.
They agree. For n = 1, 16·D + 2·D = 18·D. o_cs_n rises at A+17·D, the minimum gap is D, so the next acceptance is at A+18·D. The lead D is already counted inside the 16·D span.
The current i_cpol is used. While i_rst_n = 0, o_sclk equals the current i_cpol and follows it combinationally. On reset during a transfer, o_sclk goes to i_cpol at once, not to the latched CPOL_b.

Yes. A is the acceptance edge, an edge with i_rst_n = 1, i_cmd_valid = 1 and o_cmd_ready = 1. A response handshake at A+16·D is an edge where o_rsp_valid and i_rsp_ready are both 1, in the cycle ending at that edge.
Reset assertion is asynchronous: outputs take reset values at once on i_rst_n falling, without waiting for an i_clk edge, even mid half period. Release is synchronous to i_clk.

The documents do not say whether CFG-MIN or CFG-MAX must run full-length bursts. VER-002 sets burst lengths 1, 2 and at least 16 without tying them to a configuration. CFG-MAX is said to use 'short bursts' with no definition of short. CFG-MIN has no burst-length restriction. The designer must decide the burst lengths per configuration.
Yes. The formula f(i_clk)/(2·D) is general for D = 1 to 255. The table gives 6.25 MHz for D = 4 and about 98.04 kHz for D = 255 at 50 MHz.

The documents give no testbench mechanism or offset for driving assertion between i_clk edges. ENV-001 allows asynchronous assertion, ENV-007 forbids assertion at an edge, and VER-007 requires assertion between edges. These are consistent, but the exact time offset in simulation is left to the designer.

Yes. i_rst_n is driven to 0 from time zero, before the first rising edge, for at least 2 cycles, so it is defined. Outputs before the first assertion are undefined and unchecked. All inputs must always be 0 or 1, never X or Z.

No conflict. During reset o_cs_n = 1, so o_sclk follows i_cpol through the one permitted combinational path used while o_cs_n = 1 or in reset. The 'from a flip-flop' rule applies only while o_cs_n = 0, where o_sclk is registered from CPOL_b.
Only 'worst-case corner' in GF180MCU at 50 MHz is stated. The specific PVT (process, voltage, temperature) corner is not given and must be chosen by the designer.

o_rsp_valid is the registered value in the cycle ending at the edge, i.e. before that edge's update. If it was 0, or a response handshake occurs at that edge, the byte is loaded into o_rsp_data. Otherwise the byte becomes the held byte. The held byte is kept internally while i_rsp_ready = 0. Neither the shown nor the held byte is overwritten, and o_rsp_valid stays 1. At the handshake the held byte loads into o_rsp_data and o_rsp_valid stays 1.

This holds for all D. In Idle, o_cmd_ready = 0 in the first D−1 cycles after o_cs_n rose (cycles R to R+D−2), and NOT o_rsp_valid from cycle R+D−1 on. For D = 1 there are no blocked cycles, so it equals NOT o_rsp_valid from the cycle o_cs_n rises.

No. After reset release there are no blocked cycles. The master is in Idle with the gap requirement deemed met, and accepts a command at the first edge with i_rst_n = 1 (o_cmd_ready = 1 since o_rsp_valid = 0). The D−1 blocked cycles apply only after o_cs_n rises at the end of a burst. The gap is not guaranteed across reset.
